newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt-Turkey gas pipeline remains possibility.
newsitem.headline: Egypt-Turkey gas pipeline remains possibility.

text.p: A pipeline to take natural gas from Egypt to Turkey remains under discussion, alongside plans to export Egyptian liquefied natural gas by tanker, Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi said on Tuesday.

Banbi told a news conference that the liquefaction plant for which a site has been chosen west of Port Said would handle only four billion cubic metres of gas a year, less than half of the 10 billion cubic metres the companies are talking about.
Amoco Corp of the United States and the Italian oil company Agip are negotiating the details with Turkey.
"There are some talks about expanding (from four billion) because in Turkey they mentioned they probably will require another train (of LNG tankers)," he said.
"Instead of expanding the plant to become eight billion cubic metres, maybe the other four billion may be transported by pipeline but this is still being discussed," he added.
Amoco said in a statement on Monday that it expected to start deliveries to Turkey in the year 2001.
When it signed a memorandum of understanding with the Turkish company Botas in Cairo last November, the parties said the plan was to start exporting in 2000.
